source.name: Persona Research — Identity Fraud Control Matrix

stages.name: Session and environment
stages.blurb: The runtime the verification opens in, before any capture
stages.note: Everything at this stage is asserted by the client. It is where an adversary prepares the ground for a later technique rather than attacking the evidence itself, which is why these signals are treated as risk indicators rather than proof.
stages.assumes: the device and session are what they claim to be

stages.name: Presentation at capture
stages.blurb: Artifacts held up in front of a real camera
stages.note: This is the stage ISO/IEC 30107-3 addresses. The sensor is genuinely the source of the image, so sample-analysis signals apply in full and a laboratory result is meaningful evidence about this column.
stages.assumes: the face or document in front of the camera is real

stages.name: Capture path compromise
stages.blurb: The camera is bypassed or replaced
stages.note: This stage invalidates the assumption every sample-analysis family rests on: that the image is what the camera saw. A presentation attack detection result says nothing about this column, however strong it is.
stages.assumes: the image is what the camera saw

stages.name: Transport and submission
stages.blurb: Between the client and the service
stages.note: Attacks here do not need to produce convincing media at all. They reuse or substitute media that was already accepted. Session binding rather than image analysis is what closes them.
stages.assumes: what arrives is what this session captured

stages.name: Evidence and identity
stages.blurb: What is claimed, not how it was captured
stages.note: A technique at this stage can pass every capture and biometric control, because nothing about the capture is wrong. The evidence itself is what is false, or belongs to someone else.
stages.assumes: the evidence is genuine, and it belongs to them

stages.name: Post-decision lifecycle
stages.note: Outside the verification event entirely. Every control in the earlier columns returned a correct result; what changed is who controls the account. Only lifecycle monitoring reaches this stage.
stages.assumes: the person who verified still holds the account

controls.name: Guided capture
controls.desc: Framing, distance, and lighting guidance so correctable problems are resolved before submission.
controls.limit: Requires a Persona-controlled capture surface. Does not apply to a server-supplied image.

controls.name: Ordered frame retention
controls.desc: Frames retained in order with relative timing, so motion and temporal analysis is possible at all.
controls.limit: A single-still integration removes this and the signal families that depend on it.

controls.name: Capture-time challenge
controls.desc: A value chosen by the server after the session opens, such as a lighting pattern, a movement, or an on-screen target, which prepared media cannot have anticipated.
controls.limit: Adds friction and needs an accessible alternative. Simple challenges can be performed live by current tooling.

controls.name: Platform attestation
controls.desc: A signed statement from the operating system or app ecosystem about device integrity and application authenticity.
controls.limit: Requires a native app on a supported platform. Not available in a browser flow.

controls.name: Camera and driver enumeration
controls.desc: Enumeration of camera devices and identification of virtual, redirected, or software-backed sources.
controls.limit: Determined adversaries can present a virtual source that reports plausibly.

controls.name: Runtime environment assessment
controls.desc: Indicators of emulation, virtualization, rooting or jailbreaking, instrumentation frameworks, and repackaged applications.
controls.limit: Normal for researchers, developers, and some privacy-conscious users. A risk indicator, not proof.

controls.name: Sensor metadata plausibility
controls.desc: Whether declared resolution, optical characteristics, and encoding are mutually consistent and consistent with the claimed device.
controls.limit: Metadata can be forged; strength comes from internal consistency across many fields at once.

controls.name: Frame timing analysis
controls.desc: Injected media frequently has a cadence too regular, too fast, or otherwise inconsistent with a live sensor under real conditions.
controls.limit: Needs a frame sequence. Poor network conditions produce legitimate irregularity.

controls.name: Session binding
controls.desc: Media bound server-side to the session it was captured in, so a valid submission cannot be reused in another session or against another identity.
controls.limit: Closes replay, not first-use submission of prepared media.

controls.name: Transport protection
controls.desc: Integrity and confidentiality protection in transit, so substitution requires compromising the client rather than the connection.
controls.limit: Does not address a compromised client, which is the more common case.

controls.name: Document authenticity analysis
controls.desc: Classification, template and layout consistency, typography, security elements, and digital or physical tamper detection.
controls.limit: Can only assess what a camera can see. A well-made counterfeit reproduces exactly that.

controls.name: Encoded data validation
controls.desc: MRZ and barcode structure, checksums, formatting, and consistency between visible and machine-readable zones.
controls.limit: Present only on documents that carry an encoded zone.

controls.name: Cryptographic credential validation
controls.desc: Chip or wallet credential signature verified against a trust chain rooted in the issuing authority, with data-group integrity checked.
controls.limit: Confirms issuance, not issuance quality, current status, or who is presenting it.

controls.name: Authoritative source corroboration
controls.desc: Claimed attributes compared against records held by an issuing authority or another source reliable for the use case.
controls.limit: Coverage is thinner for younger people, recent arrivals, and thin-file populations. Breached attributes may also be known to an attacker.

controls.name: Face comparison
controls.desc: Similarity between the live capture and a trusted reference, assessed at an operating point chosen for the use case.
controls.limit: Inherits the assurance of the reference. A comparison against a forgery confirms a resemblance to a forgery.

controls.name: Liveness and PAD ensemble
controls.desc: Specialized components across signal families A to G, combined into a calibrated result with reason categories.
controls.limit: Assumes the image is what the camera saw. Not an injection control.

controls.name: Device and network context
controls.desc: Device profile and novelty, connection origin, anonymization services, hosting providers, and consistency with prior sessions.
controls.limit: Probabilistic. Legitimate users travel, use privacy tools, and share infrastructure.

controls.name: Velocity and repeated artifacts
controls.desc: How often an attribute, document, biometric reference, device, or derived artifact recurs within a defined window.
controls.limit: Base rates vary by population. Households, public terminals, and assisted onboarding all produce legitimate recurrence.

controls.name: Link and graph analysis
controls.desc: Relationships across accounts and transactions, such as a shared face under different identities, one document across accounts, or common infrastructure and backgrounds.
controls.limit: Identifies relationships, not culpability. A ring that keeps attempts separate produces fewer edges.

controls.name: Risk intelligence matching
controls.desc: Comparison against known compromised, specimen, fraudulent, or customer-supplied risk information.
controls.limit: Depends on freshness. A match describes an artifact, not necessarily the person presenting it.

controls.name: Human review
controls.desc: An escalation path for ambiguous, high-impact, or novel cases, with role-based access and auditable actions.
controls.limit: People are worse than models at judging well-made spoofs and borderline face matches. Scope review to judgments humans improve.

controls.name: Lifecycle monitoring
controls.desc: Post-verification behavior, reverification triggers, and transaction controls that can revise a completed outcome.
controls.limit: Detects after the fact. Requires the customer to define what happens on a downstream notification.

controls.name: Proportionate step-up
controls.desc: Requesting stronger or additional evidence when risk is elevated or existing evidence is insufficient for the transaction.
controls.limit: Friction has a measurable abandonment cost, distributed unevenly across a population.

controls.name: Monitored exception path
controls.desc: A documented alternative route with human adjudication for people who cannot complete the standard flow, with its own controls and its own monitoring.
controls.limit: An unmonitored exception path tends to become the path attackers use, which is why it is listed as a control against the techniques that target it.

signals.name: Material and texture response
signals.desc: Living skin scatters light beneath its surface and produces a characteristic distribution of fine texture, pore structure, and diffuse and specular reflection. Paper, glass, and silicone do not reproduce this faithfully at close range.
signals.weakens: resolution is low, compression is aggressive, the capture is distant, or the attacker picks matte materials and flattening light.

signals.name: Display and frequency artifacts
signals.desc: A screen replayed to a camera introduces artifacts a real scene does not: interference between the display grid and the sensor grid, banding from refresh rate against exposure, uneven backlight, clipped blacks, and bezel geometry.
signals.weakens: the attacker uses a high-density, high-refresh display, controls the angle, or crops out every device edge.

signals.name: Illumination and reflection consistency
signals.desc: Corneal highlights, shadow geometry across nose and brow, and light falloff are mutually consistent on a real face in a lit room. Where the flow controls the screen it can illuminate with a value chosen at capture time and check the reflected response.
signals.weakens: ambient light is very low or very strong, or the user wears glasses. Needs calibration across skin tones so sensitivity does not vary by group.

signals.name: Depth, parallax, and geometry
signals.desc: A flat artifact yields a flat scene. Small natural head movement produces relative displacement between near and far landmarks and a defocus gradient across the face; both are absent or wrong for a print or a screen.
signals.weakens: only a single still exists, no depth data is available, or the instrument is genuinely three-dimensional, as a fitted mask is.

signals.name: Motion and temporal consistency
signals.desc: Across ordered frames a live capture shows coherent landmark trajectories, continuous involuntary micro-motion, and plausible blink dynamics. Replayed and edited media often show loop points, duplicated frames, cuts, or motion too smooth to be human.
signals.weakens: the integration submits a single image rather than a sequence, which removes this family entirely.

signals.name: Anomalous signals
signals.desc: Anomaly detection identifies clusters of similar visual features across transactions and populations to reveal unusual or coordinated patterns. Effective against emerging synthetic media engines and new spoofing techniques, because it detects repeated characteristics without requiring every attack type to have been observed in advance.
signals.weakens: attacks are isolated, occur at low volume, or are distributed across long periods, conditions that reduce the clustering density needed to separate a coordinated pattern from normal variation.

signals.name: Generative and manipulation artifacts
signals.desc: Synthesized and swapped media leave traces of construction: blending seams at jaw and hairline, inconsistent detail in eyes and teeth, flicker in high-frequency regions, identity drift over a sequence, and statistical signatures from upsampling.
signals.weakens: the generator is newer than the detector. The fastest-moving family, which is why it must be paired with H.

signals.name: Capture-path and device context
signals.desc: Not image analysis at all. Which cameras the platform reports, whether a virtual driver is present, whether the runtime shows emulation or instrumentation, whether the platform will attest, whether metadata is plausible, and whether frames arrived in order.
signals.weakens: the integration supplies a finished image with no capture context, in which case none of these signals exist.

techniques.name: Emulated or virtualized device
techniques.desc: The verification is completed inside an emulator or virtual machine rather than on physical consumer hardware, giving the adversary full control of what the runtime reports and an easy path to feeding prepared media to the camera interface.
techniques.response: Treat as an elevated risk indicator rather than proof, since emulation is normal for developers and researchers. Where the flow requires it, block unsupported capture environments or step up to an alternate channel.
techniques.residual: Attestation is unavailable in browser flows, so a web integration has materially weaker evidence here than a native one.
refs: ENISA, Remote Identity Proofing: Attacks and Countermeasures

techniques.name: Rooted or jailbroken device
techniques.desc: Privilege escalation on real hardware, which lets the adversary intercept or replace the camera interface, disable client-side protections, and modify the application at runtime while otherwise presenting as a genuine device.
techniques.response: Step up to stronger evidence or a cryptographic credential, or route to review under the customer's configured policy.
techniques.residual: Detection is an arms race against concealment tooling built specifically to defeat it.

techniques.name: Repackaged application
techniques.desc: The published application is modified and re-signed so that client-side capture logic, guidance, or integrity checks behave differently while the submission still appears to come from the expected app.
techniques.response: Refuse submissions from application instances the platform will not attest to, where the integration supports attestation.
techniques.residual: Any control that relies on the client honestly describing itself is defeated here. Only platform-signed attestation resists it.

techniques.name: Instrumentation and hooking
techniques.desc: A dynamic instrumentation framework attaches to the running process to intercept function calls, alter values in memory, or substitute the frames returned by a camera API without modifying the application binary.
techniques.response: Elevated risk; combine with capture-path provenance so that substituted frames are also assessed against what a real stream looks like.
techniques.residual: Runtime detection and runtime concealment evolve together, and neither side stays ahead for long.

techniques.name: Anonymized network origin
techniques.desc: The connection is routed to obscure the true origin or to place it in a geography consistent with the claimed identity, often as part of a wider effort to make many attempts appear unrelated.
techniques.response: Weak on its own, because privacy tools are ordinary. Informative in convergence: volume from one provider, or geography inconsistent with the phone number, document country, and address at once.
techniques.residual: Residential proxy networks present as ordinary consumer connections and are hard to distinguish from them.

techniques.name: Automation harness
techniques.desc: A script or browser automation driver completes the flow, allowing many attempts to be submitted quickly and allowing the adversary to probe systematically for the boundary of a control.
techniques.response: Rate-limit, require step up, and preserve the attempt pattern for analysis. Retry behavior is distinctively informative here.
techniques.residual: A patient adversary pacing attempts below threshold produces a pattern that only a long window surfaces.

techniques.name: Printed photograph
techniques.desc: A printed image of the target face is held in front of the camera. The lowest-cost presentation attack, and still common because the source image is often freely available from social media or a stolen document.
techniques.response: Retry with guided capture where the result is ambiguous; decline or review where the outcome is confident and the flow requires it.
techniques.residual: Very low-resolution or heavily compressed captures suppress exactly the texture cues this depends on.

techniques.name: Screen replay
techniques.desc: A photograph or video of the target is replayed on a second display and filmed by the capture device, which can satisfy naive motion checks because the replayed subject genuinely moves and blinks.
techniques.response: Decline or route to review under policy. Where the signal is weak, a capture-time challenge the recording cannot anticipate resolves it.
techniques.residual: A high-density, high-refresh display at a controlled angle with the bezel cropped out suppresses the strongest cues in family B.

techniques.name: Wearable mask
subs: Paper mask with eye and mouth apertures
techniques.desc: The adversary wears a representation of the target face, which defeats depth and parallax analysis because the instrument is genuinely three-dimensional and genuinely moves with a living wearer.
techniques.response: Decline where confident. Step up to a cryptographic credential with holder binding where the flow supports it.
techniques.residual: The family that resists this best is material and texture response, which weakens under poor optics, distance, and aggressive compression.

techniques.name: Three-dimensional face model
techniques.desc: A physical model of the target head is presented to the camera. Higher effort than a mask and less flexible, but it satisfies geometry checks and can be reused across many attempts.
techniques.response: Decline. A static model fails temporal and motion analysis even when it satisfies depth.
techniques.residual: Rare in practice because the effort is poorly matched to the return, but relevant for high-value targeted attacks.

techniques.name: Generated face re-filmed
techniques.desc: A synthesized or face-swapped video is rendered, displayed, and filmed by the real capture device. This combines the flexibility of generative media with a genuine camera path, so capture-integrity signals show nothing wrong.
techniques.response: Step up to stronger evidence or a cryptographic credential, review, or decline. Population signals often reveal reuse across attempts.
techniques.residual: Generative artifact detection degrades as generators improve, and this technique deliberately hides behind a legitimate capture path.
refs: ENISA, Remote Identity Proofing: Attacks and Countermeasures

techniques.name: Counterfeit document at camera
techniques.desc: A fabricated or altered document is presented to the camera during document capture, relying on the fact that visual analysis can only assess what the camera can see.
techniques.response: Request recapture where quality is the issue; step up to issuing source or chip validation where authenticity is the question.
techniques.residual: A well-made counterfeit reproduces the visible design faithfully. Cryptographic or source validation is what introduces evidence the forger does not control.

techniques.name: Virtual camera driver
techniques.desc: Software registers itself as a camera device and supplies prepared media to any application that opens it. The most accessible injection technique, because consumer tools for it exist for legitimate streaming purposes.
techniques.response: Block unsupported capture paths, step up to an alternate channel, or decline. Content analysis alone does not address this.
techniques.residual: Where the integration supplies a finished image with no capture context, none of the family H signals exist at all.

techniques.name: Hooked camera API
techniques.desc: On a compromised device, calls to the platform camera interface are intercepted and the returned frames replaced, so the application receives adversary-supplied media through what appears to be the normal path.
techniques.response: Refuse or step up where the platform will not attest to the device and application instance.
techniques.residual: This is precisely the case platform attestation exists for, and precisely the case where a browser integration cannot obtain it.

techniques.name: Hardware capture device
techniques.desc: A physical device presents itself to the host as a webcam while replaying prepared video, defeating software-only inspection because the operating system genuinely sees a hardware camera.
techniques.response: Assess sensor metadata plausibility and frame cadence; a capture-time challenge the prepared media cannot anticipate is the strongest single control.
techniques.residual: The most resistant injection technique to software inspection, and the reason capture-time challenge values matter.

techniques.name: Real-time face swap
subs: Live swap onto the operator's face
techniques.desc: Generative software transforms the operator's live video into the target identity in real time and injects the result, so the media responds to instructions and challenges as they are issued.
techniques.response: Step up to a cryptographic credential with holder binding, review, or decline. Combine generative artifact analysis with capture-path evidence.
techniques.residual: The fastest-evolving technique in the matrix. Detection that recognizes current generators degrades predictably as new ones appear.
refs: ENISA, Remote Identity Proofing: Attacks and Countermeasures

techniques.name: Emulator fed prepared media
techniques.desc: An emulated device is configured so that its virtual camera returns a prepared video file, combining the environment technique at AT01 with injection at AT03 into a single low-cost workflow.
techniques.response: Block unsupported environments where the flow requires a trustworthy capture path.
techniques.residual: Cheap, scriptable, and easy to run at volume, which makes velocity and graph signals unusually productive against it.

techniques.name: Payload substitution in transit
techniques.desc: The captured media is replaced between the client and the service, so a genuine capture session produces a submission the adversary chose.
techniques.response: Reject submissions that are not integrity-bound to the session that produced them.
techniques.residual: Transport protection moves the problem to the client; a compromised client remains the more common route.

techniques.name: Session replay
techniques.desc: A previously successful submission is resubmitted, either in a new session or against a different identity, on the assumption that media accepted once will be accepted again.
techniques.response: Bind media server-side to its session and treat recurrence of an identical artifact across identities as a population signal.
techniques.residual: Requires the adversary to have obtained a valid prior submission, which itself indicates a separate compromise.

techniques.name: Direct submission with no capture
techniques.desc: A finished image is supplied to the service through an integration path that does not involve a Persona-controlled capture, so no capture context exists to describe.
techniques.response: Content analysis still applies. Injection resistance in the sense used here does not, and any claim about it should be qualified accordingly.
techniques.residual: This is the single most consequential configuration choice for injection resistance, and it is a customer decision.

techniques.name: Cross-identity media reuse
techniques.desc: The same face capture or document image is submitted against multiple distinct claimed identities, often across accounts or over an extended period to stay below velocity thresholds.
techniques.response: Recurrence of a biometric reference or document number across distinct identities is far more diagnostic than recurrence of a network address; thresholds should reflect that.
techniques.residual: Only visible across transactions. A single submission carries no evidence of it.

techniques.name: Fabricated document
techniques.desc: A document that was never legitimately issued, produced from a template or generated to order. Quality ranges from obviously wrong to close reproductions of current designs.
techniques.response: Request alternate evidence or source corroboration, then review or decline. Version consistency is productive: a layout retired before the stated issue date is wrong however well made.
techniques.residual: Visual analysis cannot establish with certainty that a physical document was legitimately issued.

techniques.name: Altered genuine document
techniques.desc: A real document modified so that it supports a different identity or different attributes, most commonly a replaced portrait or an altered date, name, or number.
techniques.response: Step up to issuing source or chip validation, which compares the visible page against signed data the forger cannot alter.
techniques.residual: Digital and physical alteration leave different traces; a deployment that assesses only one covers only part of this technique.

techniques.name: Stolen genuine document
techniques.desc: Authentic, unaltered evidence belonging to another person. Every document control returns a correct result, because there is nothing wrong with the document.
techniques.response: Binding is the control that matters. Require face comparison against the document or chip portrait, and check compromised-evidence intelligence.
techniques.residual: A document recorded as compromised may be presented by its rightful holder, which argues for review rather than automatic decline.

techniques.name: Specimen or published template
techniques.desc: A specimen document published by an issuer for reference purposes, or a widely circulated template image, submitted as if it were a real credential.
techniques.response: Decline. These circulate widely and are a recurring source of low-effort attempts, often in volume from one source.
techniques.residual: Intelligence about circulating artifacts ages, and a new specimen circulates before it is recorded.

techniques.name: Synthetic identity
techniques.desc: An identity assembled from a mix of real and fabricated attributes, sometimes cultivated over months so that it accumulates a plausible data footprint before it is used.
techniques.response: Corroborate against authoritative sources, weigh phone and email tenure, and examine relationship structure. Thin or conflicting history is the usual tell.
techniques.residual: A patiently cultivated identity can satisfy attribute corroboration. Tenure is what an adversary cannot create on demand, and what a cultivated identity buys.

techniques.name: Compromised authoritative data
techniques.desc: The record a verification corroborates against is itself wrong, either because an issuing process was compromised or because breached personal data allows an adversary to satisfy knowledge-style checks.
techniques.response: Do not treat corroboration as proof that the presenter is the rightful individual. Require binding, and route conflicts to human judgment.
techniques.residual: If an issuing process was compromised, the resulting document is authentic. Cryptography confirms issuance and cannot assess the quality of it.

techniques.name: Identity muling
techniques.desc: A real person completes the verification with their own genuine evidence, then transfers control of the account. Every capture, document, and biometric control returns a correct result.
techniques.response: Address after the fact through lifecycle monitoring, transaction controls, and investigation of related activity.
techniques.residual: The structural limit of biometric binding. A genuinely present, genuinely matching person cannot be detected at the verification event.
refs: Persona Research, Identity muling and second-party fraud

techniques.name: Account takeover
techniques.desc: Control of an existing verified account is obtained through credential compromise, session theft, or social engineering, inheriting the assurance of the original verification.
techniques.response: Step up authentication or identity verification on device novelty, geography change, and recent SIM swap indicators.
techniques.residual: Identity proofing establishes a link at one moment. It does not describe who controls the account afterwards.

techniques.name: Recovery path abuse
techniques.desc: The account recovery flow is attacked instead of onboarding, because recovery is frequently configured as a weaker path while protecting an asset that has become more valuable.
techniques.response: Recovery should not establish control of an account on evidence weaker than the evidence that opened it. Recent SIM swap is particularly significant here.
techniques.residual: An adversary who cannot pass onboarding has an obvious incentive to attack recovery, and often finds a shorter path.

techniques.name: Coordinated ring at scale
subs: Dense cluster from a shared toolkit
techniques.desc: Activity distributed across many people, accounts, devices, or documents so that no single submission is anomalous. The structure connecting the attempts is the finding, not any one of them.
techniques.response: Restrict linked accounts, investigate the cluster, and refine policy. A star can often be blocked at the hub; a chain requires investigation to find its extent.
techniques.residual: The first application in a cluster has no cluster to belong to yet. It becomes suspicious only when the fourth arrives.

ladder.label: Selfie liveness only
ladder.desc: Frame retention and a liveness check. No document capture.

ladder.label: Document and selfie
ladder.desc: Adds guided capture, document authenticity, encoded data, and face comparison, over a protected connection.

ladder.label: + Capture checks
ladder.desc: Adds a capture-time challenge, camera and runtime checks, frame timing, and session binding.

ladder.label: + Evidence sources
ladder.desc: Adds chip and wallet credential validation and authoritative source checks.

ladder.label: + Context and population
ladder.desc: Adds device and network context, velocity, link analysis, and risk intelligence.

ladder.label: Full stack, web
ladder.desc: Every control a browser flow supports. Platform attestation needs a native app.

standards.name: ISO/IEC 30107-3:2023
standards.note: Testing and reporting for biometric presentation attack detection. Use for evaluation scope and metrics at stage AT02. Do not imply it covers media injection or system-level attacks.

standards.name: ISO/IEC 30107-1:2023
standards.note: The presentation attack detection framework, including the vocabulary of instruments and species used throughout this matrix.

standards.name: CEN/TS 18099:2024
standards.note: Framework for detecting and evaluating biometric data injection attacks, meaning samples replaced or modified before feature extraction. The correct counterpart to 30107-3 for stage AT03, not a substitute for it.

standards.name: ISO/IEC 19795-1:2021
standards.note: Principles and framework for biometric performance testing and reporting. Use for face comparison methodology and for the form in which error rates should be quoted.

standards.name: ISO/IEC 19795-10:2024
standards.note: Quantifying performance variation across demographic groups. The relevant reporting form is per-group error at a fixed operating point, not a single aggregate.

standards.name: ISO/IEC 29794-5
standards.note: Face image quality assessment, including component measures reported alongside a unified score. Quality conditions everything downstream of it.

standards.name: ISO/IEC 2382-37
standards.note: Harmonized biometric vocabulary. Use to fix terminology before comparing vendor claims, because much apparent disagreement is vocabulary.

standards.name: NIST SP 800-63A r4
standards.note: Identity proofing and enrollment: resolution, validation, verification, fraud checks, privacy, redress, and accessibility. Tie any assurance-level claim to a defined service, configuration, and assessment scope.

standards.name: ETSI TS 119 461
standards.note: Policy and security requirements for identity proofing service components, including the five-task operational model and the proofing record.

standards.name: ICAO Doc 9303
standards.note: Machine-readable travel documents, chip data, and the public key infrastructure behind electronic passport validation.

standards.name: ENISA remote identity proofing
standards.note: Threat analysis and good practice, including presentation attacks, deepfakes, and injection. Guidance rather than a conformance standard.

questions.ask: Which instrument species were tested, and which were not?
questions.why: A result covers only the species in the test set. Untested classes are not covered by the number, however strong it looks.

questions.ask: Presentation attacks only, or injection as well?
questions.why: Separate attack classes with separate controls, in columns AT02 and AT03 of this matrix. A result about one is not evidence about the other.

questions.ask: Which devices, operating systems, and capture modes?
questions.why: Camera quality, available sensors, and platform integrity features vary enormously. Results do not transfer across device classes.
A single still removes the motion and temporal families entirely, which materially changes what is detectable.

questions.ask: At what operating point, and what was the paired error rate?
questions.why: Either error rate can be made to look excellent by sacrificing the other. Both are needed.

questions.ask: Which population, and was error reported by group?
questions.why: Aggregates can conceal materially worse performance for a subgroup. ISO/IEC 19795-10 addresses this.
Both models and attacks change. A result ages, and results against generative attacks age fastest.
Laboratory testing gives comparability under controlled conditions; production monitoring gives evidence about the real distribution. Neither substitutes for the other.

sections.name: Verification checks
sections.blurb: The per-submission checks that decide whether a verification passes
sections.note: Each check is configured as required or non-required per template, so the same check contributes differently in two deployments. Results are Passed, Failed, or Not Applicable.

sections.name: Reports
sections.blurb: Lookups against external and authoritative data, run beside a verification
sections.note: A report describes a record, not the person in front of the camera. Coverage varies by geography and by how thin the subject file is.

sections.name: Signals
sections.blurb: Environment, behaviour, and population measurements exposed per inquiry
sections.note: Signals are evidence, not decisions. Most are individually weak and only become diagnostic in convergence, which is why they are exposed as values rather than as verdicts.

sections.name: Graph
sections.blurb: Relationships between accounts and the properties they share
sections.note: Graph identifies relationships, not culpability. The first account in a cluster has no cluster to belong to yet.

sections.name: Marketplace integrations
sections.blurb: Third-party services called from a workflow
sections.note: Listed here is the fraud- and identity-relevant subset of the catalogue. Marketplace integrations are available to Enterprise and managed Growth customers, and each carries its own coverage and contract.

sections.name: Inquiry configuration
sections.blurb: Template and integration settings that move the attack surface
sections.note: These are the choices a customer makes, not capabilities Persona applies on their behalf. Several of them decide whether an entire signal family exists at all.

docs.label: Collecting passports and other IDs using NFC

capabilities.name: Government ID
capabilities.desc: Detects whether the submission contains a government ID at all.

capabilities.name: Extracted properties
capabilities.desc: Detects whether the ID details the template requires were successfully extracted.

capabilities.name: Extraction inconsistency
capabilities.desc: Detects disagreement between details read from the front of the ID and details read from the barcode.

capabilities.name: Barcode inconsistency
capabilities.desc: Detects inconsistencies in the barcode carried on the ID.

capabilities.name: MRZ inconsistency
capabilities.desc: Detects whether the machine-readable zone is well formed for the document type.

capabilities.name: ID number format inconsistency
capabilities.desc: Detects whether the identification number is well formed for its issuing authority.

capabilities.name: Valid dates
capabilities.desc: Detects dates that violate the issuing authority’s own rules, such as a layout retired before its stated issue date.

capabilities.name: Fabrication
capabilities.desc: Detects IDs likely to be fabricated based on format and design, including camouflage passports.

capabilities.name: ID image tampering
capabilities.desc: Detects submissions altered in a photo editor.

capabilities.name: ID physical tampering
capabilities.desc: Detects physical alteration of the document itself, which leaves different traces than digital editing.

capabilities.name: Colour
capabilities.desc: Detects colours on the ID that differ from those expected for the document type.

capabilities.name: Paper detection
capabilities.desc: Detects a paper copy presented in place of the physical document.

capabilities.name: Electronic replica
capabilities.desc: Detects a document replayed from another screen or device rather than presented physically.

capabilities.name: Double side
capabilities.desc: Detects the same side of an ID submitted as both front and back.

capabilities.name: Compromised submission
capabilities.desc: Detects submissions traceable to a publicly available source, meaning specimens and circulating template images.

capabilities.name: Repeat
capabilities.desc: Detects an ID whose details and portrait match a previously submitted one.

capabilities.name: Inconsistent repeat
capabilities.desc: Detects reuse of an ID image or portrait carrying different identity details, meaning the same document under two identities.

capabilities.name: ID-to-selfie comparison
capabilities.desc: Compares the portrait on the ID against the selfie.

capabilities.name: Portrait age
capabilities.desc: Detects a mismatch between the age printed on the ID and the age estimated from its portrait.

capabilities.name: Public figure
capabilities.desc: Detects an ID portrait matching a known public figure.

capabilities.name: Inquiry comparison
capabilities.desc: Compares ID details such as name and birthdate against what was claimed on the inquiry.

capabilities.name: Account comparison
capabilities.desc: Compares ID details against the account they are presented for, which is a reverification rather than a first-inquiry control.

capabilities.name: Video quality
capabilities.desc: Assesses whether captured video meets the quality the downstream analysis needs.

capabilities.name: Processable submission
capabilities.desc: Detects submissions that cannot be processed, which is the usual result of an upload path with no capture behind it.

capabilities.name: Allowed ID type
capabilities.desc: Rejects document types the template does not accept, which retires out-of-circulation layouts as well.

capabilities.name: Selfie liveness
capabilities.desc: Detects whether the selfie is a live individual rather than a recording, a picture, or another spoof.

capabilities.name: Suspicious entity
capabilities.desc: Detects a government ID held up where a face should be.

capabilities.name: Multiple faces
capabilities.desc: Detects different faces across the captured poses.

capabilities.name: Pose position
capabilities.desc: Detects whether the face is correctly positioned across every requested pose, which is the response to a capture-time instruction.

capabilities.name: Pose repeat
capabilities.desc: Detects poses that are exact repeats of one another, as prepared media tends to be.

capabilities.name: Selfie repeat
capabilities.desc: Detects a selfie already on file against a different account.

capabilities.name: Selfie-to-ID comparison
capabilities.desc: Compares the selfie against the portrait on the government ID.

capabilities.name: Account comparison
capabilities.desc: Compares the selfie against the portrait already held for the account.

capabilities.name: Face covering
capabilities.desc: Detects a covered face, which suppresses the texture and geometry cues everything else depends on.

capabilities.name: Portrait quality
capabilities.desc: Assesses whether the face portrait is clear and in focus; it conditions almost every other selfie check.

capabilities.name: Video quality
capabilities.desc: Assesses selfie video integrity and quality, without which motion and temporal analysis has nothing to read.

capabilities.name: Public figure
capabilities.desc: Detects a selfie matching a known public figure.

capabilities.name: Enhanced fraud detection
capabilities.desc: Aggregates the enhanced document fraud indicators into one result alongside a composite risk score.

capabilities.name: Synthetic content detection
capabilities.desc: Detects placeholder entities and mock details of the kind that appear on demonstration and test documents.

capabilities.name: Template detection
capabilities.desc: Detects a document built from a fraudulent template circulating online.

capabilities.name: Copy-move detection
capabilities.desc: Detects evidence of copy-move forgery, where a region of the document has been duplicated over another.

capabilities.name: Image suspicious metadata
capabilities.desc: Detects irregular or post-hoc modification timestamps on a submitted image.

capabilities.name: JPEG original image detection
capabilities.desc: Detects JPEG compression inconsistencies that indicate the image was modified after capture.

capabilities.name: PDF editor detection
capabilities.desc: Detects traces of a document editor in a submitted PDF.

capabilities.name: PDF abnormal font detection
capabilities.desc: Detects fonts that are outliers relative to the rest of the document, a common sign an editor was used.

capabilities.name: Recency
capabilities.desc: Detects whether the document is recent enough for the use case, which an old but genuine document is not.

capabilities.name: Document selfie comparison
capabilities.desc: Compares a portrait carried on a supporting document against the selfie.

capabilities.name: PKI validation
capabilities.desc: Validates the document-signing and certificate-authority chain behind an NFC credential.

capabilities.name: Data tampering
capabilities.desc: Validates chip authentication and the data-group hashes on an ICAO-compliant travel document.

capabilities.name: Compromised NFC document
capabilities.desc: Detects unambiguous compromise signals: risky-list matches, hash integrity failures, a missing expected CSCA, revoked certificates.

capabilities.name: Attribute comparison
capabilities.desc: Compares chip-held details such as name and birthdate against what was claimed.

capabilities.name: Allowed issuer
capabilities.desc: Validates that a verifiable credential was issued by a trusted issuer and, for Persona-issued credentials, that its binding claims match the allowlist.

capabilities.name: Credential account comparison
capabilities.desc: Compares claims carried in a verifiable credential against the account’s own fields.

capabilities.name: SIM verification
capabilities.desc: Confirms the SIM behind a phone number through silent network authentication, without a code the user could forward.

capabilities.name: Identity comparison
capabilities.desc: Detects whether the claimed identity matches a record in an authoritative or issuing database.

capabilities.name: 2+2 detection
capabilities.desc: Requires claimed attributes to corroborate across more than one independent source rather than one.

capabilities.name: Alive detection
capabilities.desc: Detects whether the person on the matched record is living.

capabilities.name: Database face comparison
capabilities.desc: Compares the submitted selfie against a portrait held by the database source, which is a reference the presenter does not control.

capabilities.name: Inquiry comparison
capabilities.desc: Detects inconsistency between attributes on the inquiry and those submitted for lookup.

capabilities.name: Deliverable address
capabilities.desc: Detects whether the claimed address is deliverable, which a fabricated one frequently is not.

capabilities.name: AAMVA identity comparison
capabilities.desc: Compares licence attributes against participating US motor-vehicle records.

capabilities.name: eCBSV record matched
capabilities.desc: Matches name, birthdate, and social security number against Social Security Administration records.

capabilities.name: eCBSV death record
capabilities.desc: Detects that the matched social security number belongs to a deceased person.

capabilities.name: TIN name comparison
capabilities.desc: Confirms a legal name against IRS taxpayer-identification records.

capabilities.name: Serpro face comparison
capabilities.desc: Compares the submitted face against Brazil’s Serpro records.

capabilities.name: Aadhaar face comparison
capabilities.desc: Compares the submitted selfie against the portrait held in the Aadhaar database.

capabilities.name: Carrier last name
capabilities.desc: Compares the claimed surname against telecommunications-carrier records for the number.

capabilities.name: Carrier age threshold
capabilities.desc: Tests carrier-derived age against a configured threshold.

capabilities.name: Phone code confirmation
capabilities.desc: Confirms possession of the number by comparing the submitted code against the one sent to it.

capabilities.name: Phone deliverability
capabilities.desc: Detects delivery problems for the number, including landlines where a mobile is required.

capabilities.name: Email code confirmation
capabilities.desc: Confirms control of the address by comparing the submitted code against the one emailed to it.

capabilities.name: Confirmation code timeout
capabilities.desc: Requires the confirmation code to be submitted inside the allotted window, which bounds relay and guessing.

capabilities.name: Business identity comparison
capabilities.desc: Detects whether the claimed business matches a record in an authoritative registry.

capabilities.name: Active business detection
capabilities.desc: Detects whether the business is legally active rather than dissolved or lapsed.

capabilities.name: Associated persons comparison
capabilities.desc: Detects whether the declared officers and owners appear on the authoritative record.

capabilities.name: Registered agent address
capabilities.desc: Detects a submitted business address that is really the registered agent’s, a recurring shell-company pattern.

capabilities.name: Business footprint identity comparison
capabilities.desc: Corroborates a business against commercial and digital-presence data rather than registry data alone.

capabilities.name: Domain age detection
capabilities.desc: Detects a domain too young for the claimed trading history, because tenure is what an adversary cannot create on demand.

capabilities.name: Malicious website detection
capabilities.desc: Detects whether the business website is malicious.

capabilities.name: Website identity comparison
capabilities.desc: Compares information extracted from the business website against what the applicant submitted.

capabilities.name: Trademark ownership detection
capabilities.desc: Detects potential trademark conflicts in a submitted brand asset, which is how impersonation of a known brand surfaces.

capabilities.name: Profile Report
capabilities.desc: Matches authoritative identity records and returns names, birthdates, addresses, social security numbers, phones, and emails.

capabilities.name: Profile Non-Authoritative Report
capabilities.desc: Returns non-authoritative identity, contact, and address information, useful for corroboration but not for proof.

capabilities.name: Phone Risk Report
capabilities.desc: Returns carrier, line type, location, risk score, and SIM-swap risk for a phone number.

capabilities.name: Email Address Report
capabilities.desc: Assesses validity, deliverability, domain age, breach exposure, disposability, and reputation for an email address.

capabilities.name: Address Lookup Report
capabilities.desc: Standardises an address and reports deliverability, vacancy, activity, and addressee matching.

capabilities.name: Social Media Report
capabilities.desc: Finds social profiles associated with an individual, which is one way a cultivated identity’s thin history shows.

capabilities.name: Watchlist Report
capabilities.desc: Screens an individual against configured watchlists and returns the matched lists and entity details.

capabilities.name: Politically Exposed Person Report
capabilities.desc: Finds politically exposed person matches with positions, associates, affiliations, and sources.

capabilities.name: Adverse Media Report
capabilities.desc: Finds media associated with an individual and returns sources, names, countries, and match types.

capabilities.name: Crypto Address Watchlist Report
capabilities.desc: Screens a cryptocurrency wallet address for watchlist matches.

capabilities.name: Synthetic Report
capabilities.desc: Returns abuse, first-party synthetic, and third-party synthetic identity scores.

capabilities.name: SentiLink Scores Report
capabilities.desc: Returns third-party score names, values, versions, and reason codes for the application.

capabilities.name: Business Lookup Report
capabilities.desc: Retrieves registered-entity details, identifiers, status, addresses, officers, and registration authority data.

capabilities.name: Business Registrations Lookup Report
capabilities.desc: Returns formation details and registry records, including registration numbers, authorities, and statuses.

capabilities.name: Business Associated Persons Report
capabilities.desc: Returns associated people, positions, owners, and ownership roles for a business.

capabilities.name: Business Watchlist Report
capabilities.desc: Screens a business against configured sanctions, warning, fitness, and probity lists.

capabilities.name: Business Adverse Media Report
capabilities.desc: Finds adverse-media sources associated with a business search term.

capabilities.name: VPN detected
capabilities.desc: Whether any inquiry session was conducted through a VPN.

capabilities.name: Proxy detected
capabilities.desc: Whether any session ran through a proxy or other anonymising network.

capabilities.name: Tor detected
capabilities.desc: Whether any session was detected using Tor.

capabilities.name: Network threat level
capabilities.desc: Network risk scored from IP metadata, reported low, medium, or high.

capabilities.name: Risk level
capabilities.desc: Risk from the volume of recent activity observed on the IP address.

capabilities.name: IP burst
capabilities.desc: How many other completed inquiries share the same IP address inside a two-hour window.

capabilities.name: IP connection types
capabilities.desc: Connection types across sessions, such as residential, corporate, and mobile, which is how residential proxying tends to show.

capabilities.name: IP prefix /24
capabilities.desc: The /24 network prefix of the most recent session address, which groups attempts a single address would not.

capabilities.name: Session ASNs
capabilities.desc: Autonomous system numbers collected from session IP addresses, which identify hosting and proxy infrastructure.

capabilities.name: Country comparison
capabilities.desc: Whether every session occurred in the same country as the address stated on the inquiry.

capabilities.name: Impossible travel geolocation
capabilities.desc: Probability that two session locations are too far apart to have been travelled between in the elapsed time.

capabilities.name: Geolocation language mismatch
capabilities.desc: Whether the locale chosen in the last session disagrees with the country inferred from session location.

capabilities.name: TLS certificate fingerprint
capabilities.desc: Fingerprint of the TLS certificate the client observed, which surfaces interception between client and service.

capabilities.name: Rooted device detected
capabilities.desc: Whether the user holds root access on the device used for verification.

capabilities.name: Device or app tampering
capabilities.desc: Whether technologies used to modify the app, SDK, or operating system were detected in any session.

capabilities.name: Apple app attestation
capabilities.desc: Verifies iOS app integrity, flagging requests that come from a suspicious app version.

capabilities.name: Google Play Integrity
capabilities.desc: Verifies Android app integrity and reports the highest device integrity level across sessions.

capabilities.name: Bundle names
capabilities.desc: Application bundle identifiers seen across sessions, flagged as anomalous where the template pins one.

capabilities.name: User agent spoof attempts
capabilities.desc: Count of sessions whose device or browser information was masked, altered, or falsified.

capabilities.name: Request spoof attempts
capabilities.desc: Count of requests showing tampering or manipulation across all sessions.

capabilities.name: Mismatched user agent count
capabilities.desc: Distinct user agents differing from the original session’s, where a non-zero value suggests the session token moved devices.

capabilities.name: Curl request detected
capabilities.desc: Whether a device that accessed the inquiry looks like a command-line HTTP client rather than a browser.

capabilities.name: Incognito browsing detected
capabilities.desc: Whether any browser used in the inquiry was in private browsing mode.

capabilities.name: Devtools open
capabilities.desc: Whether browser developer tools were open during the flow.

capabilities.name: Unrecognised referer
capabilities.desc: Whether a session arrived from a referer outside the domains allowed on the template.

capabilities.name: Virtual camera risk level
capabilities.desc: Likelihood a virtual camera supplied pre-recorded or generated media during selfie or document capture.

capabilities.name: Virtual camera detected
capabilities.desc: Whether any virtual-camera indication was raised during the verification.

capabilities.name: Any uploaded
capabilities.desc: Whether any image was uploaded as a file rather than captured through a live camera.

capabilities.name: Camera count
capabilities.desc: Total cameras the device reported during capture, which is how an added virtual source surfaces.

capabilities.name: All camera labels
capabilities.desc: Device labels of every camera enumerated during the capture sequence.

capabilities.name: Camera frame rate
capabilities.desc: Frames per second of the selected camera, which injected media frequently reports implausibly.

capabilities.name: Camera facing mode
capabilities.desc: Which way the camera used for capture was facing.

capabilities.name: Gyroscope factor
capabilities.desc: Average gyroscope movement during capture, because a real handheld capture is never perfectly still.

capabilities.name: First image dimensions
capabilities.desc: Pixel dimensions of the first captured image, checked for consistency with the claimed device.

capabilities.name: Device name missing
capabilities.desc: Whether the session has no device name, which can indicate the verification did not come from a real device.

capabilities.name: Max selfie liveness risk level
capabilities.desc: Highest liveness risk across the inquiry’s verifications, signalling media that may be fake, altered, or generated.

capabilities.name: Bot score
capabilities.desc: Score from 0 to 100 for the likelihood the inquiry was submitted by a bot.

capabilities.name: Behaviour threat level
capabilities.desc: Behaviour risk summarised from network, device, and user-behaviour evidence.

capabilities.name: Behaviour anomaly
capabilities.desc: Unsupervised modelling that flags groups of inquiries anomalous at population level rather than individually.

capabilities.name: Session count
capabilities.desc: How many sessions were started before the inquiry completed; three or more can mean several devices.

capabilities.name: Sessions geolocation delta
capabilities.desc: Largest distance between two session locations on the same inquiry.

capabilities.name: Time to complete
capabilities.desc: Seconds between verification creation and submission; very short durations suggest automated submission.

capabilities.name: Shortcut pastes
capabilities.desc: Count of keyboard paste events across sessions, which is how a supplied identity dossier is usually entered.

capabilities.name: Distraction events
capabilities.desc: How many times the user left the flow window during the inquiry.

capabilities.name: Hesitation ratio
capabilities.desc: Share of total flow time in which the user made no input.

capabilities.name: Off-hours session
capabilities.desc: Local start time of the latest session, converted using the timezone inferred from IP geolocation.

capabilities.name: Reusable persona used
capabilities.desc: Whether the end user authenticated into an existing persona rather than establishing a new one.

capabilities.name: Selfie visual cluster score
capabilities.desc: How visually similar the submitted selfie is to selfies already on file.

capabilities.name: Selfie visual cluster size
capabilities.desc: How many other selfies on file look visually identical to this one.

capabilities.name: ID vision cluster score
capabilities.desc: How closely the submitted ID resembles other IDs seen with the same layout.

capabilities.name: ID vision cluster size
capabilities.desc: How many IDs on file look visually identical to this one, which is the signature of one template used at volume.

capabilities.name: Government ID inconsistent repeat count
capabilities.desc: How many mismatches the inconsistent-repeat check found for the document.

capabilities.name: IP impossible travel
capabilities.desc: Risk that activity linked to the matched identity occurred in places too far apart for the elapsed time.

capabilities.name: Devices count
capabilities.desc: How many distinct devices are linked to the matched identity.

capabilities.name: First seen days ago
capabilities.desc: Days since the earliest recorded activity for the matched identity, which is tenure a cultivated identity has to buy.

capabilities.name: Public figure name detected
capabilities.desc: Whether the verification’s full name exactly matches a known public figure.

capabilities.name: Address street entropy
capabilities.desc: Entropy of the street address on an ID; repeating or sequential digits suggest a fabricated address.

capabilities.name: Inquiry velocity
capabilities.desc: Inquiries created on the account inside a configured window; high velocity suggests automated abuse.

capabilities.name: Failed inquiries count
capabilities.desc: How many inquiries on the account were declined, which is how boundary-probing shows.

capabilities.name: Device count
capabilities.desc: How many distinct devices are associated with the account.

capabilities.name: Address update count
capabilities.desc: How many times account address fields changed inside a configured window.

capabilities.name: List match count
capabilities.desc: Watchlist, sanctions, and block-list matches associated directly with the account.

capabilities.name: New mobile device used during reverification
capabilities.desc: Whether a device in this inquiry has not appeared in the account’s five most recent completed inquiries.

capabilities.name: Device fingerprint
capabilities.desc: Any device fingerprint collected during one of the account’s inquiries.

capabilities.name: Browser fingerprint
capabilities.desc: Any browser fingerprint collected during one of the account’s inquiries.

capabilities.name: IP address
capabilities.desc: Any IP address used while completing one of the account’s inquiries.

capabilities.name: Government ID number
capabilities.desc: Any ID number read from a government ID collected during an account inquiry.

capabilities.name: Social security number
capabilities.desc: Any social security number collected during one of the account’s inquiries.

capabilities.name: Phone number
capabilities.desc: Any phone number collected during one of the account’s inquiries.

capabilities.name: Email address
capabilities.desc: Any email address collected during one of the account’s inquiries.

capabilities.name: Address
capabilities.desc: Any primary address associated with the account’s inquiries, normalised and validated before it enters Graph.

capabilities.name: Name
capabilities.desc: The account’s full name.

capabilities.name: Birthdate
capabilities.desc: The account’s birthdate.

capabilities.name: Linked via
capabilities.desc: An edge joining two account nodes that share a property, which is the structure a ring produces and a single attempt cannot.

capabilities.name: Linked to
capabilities.desc: An edge joining an account node to a property node the account has.

capabilities.name: Cluster
capabilities.desc: A group of account nodes all linked to the same property node, which is the star pattern that can be blocked at its hub.

capabilities.name: Cluster size
capabilities.desc: The number of nodes in a cluster, which is what separates a household from a ring.

capabilities.name: Hops
capabilities.desc: Distance from a connected node to a starting node, counted in edges; a chain needs more hops than a star.

capabilities.name: Starting nodes
capabilities.desc: The initial accounts of interest in a query, which is the seed set the traversal expands from.

capabilities.name: Graph Explorer
capabilities.desc: The visual interface for running a query and exploring its results on the canvas.

capabilities.name: Query
capabilities.desc: A search defining which accounts to surface, specified by at least one property and value.

capabilities.name: Query template
capabilities.desc: A preconfigured query saved for reuse, which is how a confirmed ring pattern becomes a standing check.

capabilities.name: Maximum hops
capabilities.desc: The furthest edge distance a connected account may sit from a starting node, which bounds the traversal.

capabilities.name: LexisNexis InstantID
capabilities.desc: Retrieves identity information to corroborate a claimed identity and strengthen fraud detection.

capabilities.name: Prove
capabilities.desc: Adds phone-centric identity and possession signals to a workflow.

capabilities.name: AtData
capabilities.desc: Enriches an email identity with deliverability, activity, and fraud-risk signals.

capabilities.name: Clearbit
capabilities.desc: Enriches people and companies from an email address or domain.

capabilities.name: FullContact
capabilities.desc: Enriches an identity profile with person and contact information.

capabilities.name: MX
capabilities.desc: Verifies a bank account and compares the account-holder name against the claimed identity.

capabilities.name: VerifyMy
capabilities.desc: Adds age-assurance and identity-verification capability to a workflow.

capabilities.name: SentiLink
capabilities.desc: Returns synthetic-identity, identity-theft, and first-party fraud risk scores.

capabilities.name: Mastercard Identity
capabilities.desc: Returns identity, network, and IP risk scores from submitted identity signals.

capabilities.name: CRS Credit
capabilities.desc: Retrieves credit and identity data for verification and risk decisions.

capabilities.name: Nova Credit
capabilities.desc: Retrieves cross-border credit data, which reaches recent arrivals a domestic file does not cover.

capabilities.name: PhotoDNA
capabilities.desc: Detects known harmful imagery by comparing image hashes against PhotoDNA data.

capabilities.name: Chainalysis
capabilities.desc: Screens cryptocurrency addresses and transactions for risk from inside a workflow.

capabilities.name: TRM Labs
capabilities.desc: Screens cryptocurrency wallets and transactions for financial-crime risk.

capabilities.name: Notabene
capabilities.desc: Supports Travel Rule compliance by exchanging counterparty information for a transfer.

capabilities.name: Okta
capabilities.desc: Triggers workforce verification, retrieves user data, and automates account actions in identity management.

capabilities.name: Microsoft Entra
capabilities.desc: Adds employee profile data and identity verification to access-management workflows.

capabilities.name: Cisco Duo
capabilities.desc: Verifies workforce identity during helpdesk interactions and remote employee onboarding.

capabilities.name: Auth0
capabilities.desc: Retrieves user profiles, verified contacts, login activity, and identities for an access decision.

capabilities.name: Stytch
capabilities.desc: Retrieves authentication profiles, verified contacts, OAuth identities, and passkey registrations.

capabilities.name: Yardstik
capabilities.desc: Connects workforce background-screening information to a Persona workflow.

capabilities.name: Twilio
capabilities.desc: Retrieves SMS, messaging, and account data for use inside a workflow.

capabilities.name: Slack
capabilities.desc: Sends targeted identity-event alerts to a channel or an individual reviewer.

capabilities.name: Shopify
capabilities.desc: Pushes Persona identity signals into order-risk assessment.

capabilities.name: Anthropic
capabilities.desc: Generates summaries and decision support for a reviewer from workflow data.

capabilities.name: OpenAI
capabilities.desc: Generates text from workflow data through an action step.

capabilities.name: Capture methods
capabilities.desc: Chooses, per device type, whether the user may capture a new photo or upload an existing image.

capabilities.name: Capture a new photo
capabilities.desc: Restricting to live camera capture is what produces motion, behavioural, device, and real-time metadata at all.

capabilities.name: Upload an existing image
capabilities.desc: Permitting file upload admits images that can be reused, shared, spoofed, or edited before submission.

capabilities.name: Selfie poses: centre, left, and right
capabilities.ref: Images of individual selfie poses looking center, left, and right
capabilities.desc: Collects the default three poses, which is what liveness and three-point comparison read.

capabilities.name: Centre-only checks
capabilities.desc: Using the centre-facing selfie alone removes the pose challenge and the parallax it produces.

capabilities.name: NFC verification
capabilities.desc: Reads the chip on ICAO-compliant passports and supported identity documents through a mobile SDK integration.

doc.label: Collecting passports and other IDs using NFC

capabilities.name: Mobile SDK
capabilities.desc: A native integration, and the only model in which platform attestation is available at all.

capabilities.name: Hosted Flow
capabilities.desc: Redirects the user to a Persona-hosted verification page.

capabilities.name: Embedded Flow
capabilities.desc: Embeds the Persona interface in a website iframe; template-generated inquiries can duplicate on reload.

capabilities.name: Transactions-based integration
capabilities.desc: Uses the customer’s own capture interface, which is the configuration that removes capture context entirely.

capabilities.name: Create inquiries via API
capabilities.desc: Creating server-side prevents arbitrary mass creation and supports immutable prefilled fields.

capabilities.name: Block client-side inquiry creation
capabilities.desc: Disables client-side creation for a template, so an adversary cannot open unlimited attempts.

capabilities.name: Reference ID
capabilities.desc: Associates every inquiry for one user with the same account, which is what makes repeat detection possible.

capabilities.name: Inquiry one-time links
capabilities.desc: Grants single-use access to resume an inquiry, rather than a reusable link anyone holding it can open.

capabilities.name: Inquiry session limit
capabilities.desc: Caps how many sessions one inquiry may open, 25 by default, which bounds a captured link passed between devices.

capabilities.name: Expiration from inquiry pending
capabilities.desc: Shortens the window a started inquiry stays open, limiting how long a leaked link remains usable.

capabilities.name: One-time link expiry
capabilities.desc: Sets how long an authenticated access link stays valid.

capabilities.name: Device handoff link
capabilities.desc: Sets expiry for links that move an inquiry between devices, which should be as short as the use case tolerates.

capabilities.name: Required checks
capabilities.desc: A required check must pass for the verification to pass; the same check set behaves differently once it is non-required.

capabilities.name: Non-required checks
capabilities.desc: Records a check as context without failing the verification on it, useful while calibrating but risky as a resting state.

capabilities.name: Acceptable countries
capabilities.desc: Restricts government ID verification to selected issuing countries.

capabilities.name: Acceptable ID types
capabilities.desc: Restricts which document types the verification accepts, which retires known-weak layouts.

capabilities.name: Reject IDs previously submitted by other accounts
capabilities.ref: Whether to reject IDs that were previously submitted by other accounts in your Persona organization
capabilities.desc: Rejects a document already associated with a different account in the organisation.

capabilities.name: Require both sides of the ID
capabilities.ref: Whether to require both the front side and back side of the ID to be submitted
capabilities.desc: Collecting the back is what makes barcode and encoded-zone checks applicable rather than not applicable.

capabilities.name: Conditional step
capabilities.desc: Branches on inquiry, report, case, or account data, so a step-up fires only where risk is elevated.

capabilities.name: Run Report
capabilities.desc: Runs a report when configured conditions are met, adding evidence the capture itself cannot supply.

capabilities.name: Mark Inquiry for Review
capabilities.desc: Routes an uncertain inquiry to human judgment rather than forcing an automated decision.

capabilities.name: Create Case
capabilities.desc: Opens a case for investigation, which is where a cluster rather than a single attempt gets adjudicated.

capabilities.name: Teams
capabilities.desc: Groups reviewers and drives case-assignment policy, so review has defined ownership and an audit trail.

capabilities.name: Domain allowlist
capabilities.desc: Restricts which domains may boot the embedded flow; subdomains must be listed separately.

capabilities.name: Permissions-Policy
capabilities.desc: Controls whether the parent document grants camera access; blocking it prevents ID and selfie capture outright.

capabilities.name: Sandbox attributes
capabilities.desc: Overrides the default iframe sandbox; loosening it can impair the flow’s own security guarantees.
